Chapter 3 Solutions Here are the solutions to the exercises 3.1 Importing dta files Steps: Go to NBER Current Population Survey (CPS) Merged Outgoing Rotation Group: https://data.nber.org/morg/annual/ Download and ingest the 2024 data Use the use command to ingest the CPS data Use the list command to find the State and County of the 200th observation. What is the County and State of the 200th observation Hint: Search for County FIPS code (e.g.: https://fipsdecoder.com/county-fips-codes) use https://data.nber.org/morg/annual/morg24.dta, clear list stfips county in 200 | stfips county | |-----------------| 200. | AL 97 | +-----------------+ The 200th observation lives in Mobile County, Alabama. 3.2 Importing csv files Steps: Go to the Census Bureau’s Current Population Survey home page Download the July 2026 csv file Use the import delimited command to ingest the July 2026 CPS file What is the sex (pesex) and labor force status (pemlr) of the 50th observation? Use the CPS data dictioary: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/datasets/2026/basic/2026_Basic_CPS_Public_Use_Record_Layout_plus_IO_Code_list.txt import delimited using "https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/cps/datasets/2026/basic/jul26pub.csv", clear list pesex pemlr in 50 (encoding automatically selected: ISO-8859-1) (393 vars, 120,930 obs) +---------------+ | pesex pemlr | |---------------| 50. | 1 4 | +---------------+ The 50th observation is male, who is unemployed - looking for employment 3.3 Importing Excel files Steps: Go to St. Louis Federal Reserve Board FRED site for the unemployment rate: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE/ Download the excel file “UNRATE.xlsx” Import the excel file with the import excel command. List the unemployment and date variables What is the unemployment rate for May 2023? import excel using "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Data/UNRATE.xlsx", sheet("Monthly") clear list in 906 (2 vars, 944 obs) +-----------------+ | A B | |-----------------| 906. | 01may2023 3.6 | +-----------------+ The unemployment rate in May 2023 was 3.6% 3.4 Importing SAS files Steps: Download the NBER MEPS Panel 24 Longitudinal Data File https://data.nber.org/meps/h225/h225.sas7bdat Import the Sas file into Stata List the Person ID (DUPERSID, Year of Birth (DOBYY), and Death Status during 2019-2020 (DIED) for the first 10 observations Codebook: https://meps.ahrq.gov/mepsweb/data_stats/download_data/pufs/h225/h225cb.pdf Did any one of the first 10 observations die during 2019-2020 panel? import sas using "/Users/Sam/Desktop/Econ 643/Data/h225.sas7bdat", clear list DUPERSID DOBYY DIED in 1/10 (2,761 vars, 9,797 obs) +---------------------------+ | DUPERSID DOBYY DIED | |---------------------------| 1. | 2460002101 1945 0 | 2. | 2460004101 1941 0 | 3. | 2460004102 1941 0 | 4. | 2460005101 1994 0 | 5. | 2460005102 1993 0 | |---------------------------| 6. | 2460006101 1958 0 | 7. | 2460006102 1955 0 | 8. | 2460007101 1961 0 | 9. | 2460007102 1999 0 | 10. | 2460008101 1945 0 | +---------------------------+ None of the first 10 observations died during 2019-2020 panel. 3.5 Import an SPSS file Steps: Download the following file from Stata: https://www.stata.com/sampledata/auto.sav Use the import command to ingest an SPSS file List the first 10 observations’ make, price, and miles per gallon What is the Miles per Gallon for the second observation? import spss using "https://www.stata.com/sampledata/auto.sav" list make price mpg in 1/10 list mpg in 2 (12 vars, 74 obs) +-----------------------------+ | make price mpg | |-----------------------------| 1. | AMC Concord 4099 22 | 2. | AMC Pacer 4749 17 | 3. | AMC Spirit 3799 22 | 4. | Buick Century 4816 20 | 5. | Buick Electra 7827 15 | |-----------------------------| 6. | Buick LeSabre 5788 18 | 7. | Buick Opel 4453 26 | 8. | Buick Regal 5189 20 | 9. | Buick Riviera 10372 16 | 10. | Buick Skylark 4082 19 | +-----------------------------+ +-----+ | mpg | |-----| 2. | 17 | +-----+ The second observation has receives 17 miles per gallon.

Retrieved from https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/modules/ Note: Recommended resources UCLA OARC Stata resources: https://stats.oarc.ucla.edu/stata/modules/ I have used this source on numerous times. Even when you become proficient with Stata, UCLA’s OARC Stata resources have been very helpful. If you just type UCLA OARC Stata in a search engine, then it will usually pop up. Statalist if usually another good resource when trying to figure out what went wrong. If you ask as question on the listserve, you will likely be scolded by Nick Cox, or you will be told to “read the manual”. However, if you just read what others have asked, you will often find useful information.
